Flavio Bolsonaro, who lost Brazil's October 25 presidential run-off, has reportedly left the country for the US [File: AFP]By AP and ReutersPublished On 27 Oct 202627 Oct 2026
A senior US State Department official has said that the Trump administration will issue visas to Brazilian Senator Flavio Bolsonaro and his family, allowing them to enter the US after news outlets reported that Bolsonaro had fled Brazil following his loss in the country’s presidential election.
The news came on Tuesday, one day after Brazil’s Supreme Court ordered Bolsonaro to turn over his passports as part of a probe into alleged money laundering. Bolsonaro has denied any wrongdoing and said on Monday that he would stay in the country and lead the opposition.
Recommended Stories list of 3 itemslist 1 of 3Flavio Bolsonaro ‘will not give up’ after Brazil election resultslist 2 of 3How did Lula beat Bolsonaro after losing Brazil’s first-round election?list 3 of 3Brazil’s real sinks after Lula’s re-election victoryend of list
Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva, who has previously accused members of the Bolsonaro family of courting US interference in Brazilian affairs for their political benefit, called the right-wing senator’s actions shameful.
“This is what the Bolsonaro family is like,” Lula said. “Brazil is their second nation, the US is their first.”
Bolsonaro, the son of former right-wing president Jair Bolsonaro, initially refused to acknowledge the election results and said he would seek their annulment. His party released a statement on Monday saying it accepted the results of the election, which the conservative candidate lost by more than 4.4 million votes.

The Angerona, a crude oil tanker US President Donald Trump has said is carrying a million barrels of Venezuelan oil, is docked near the site of his campaign rally in Corpus Christi, Texas, on October 27, 2026 [AFP]By Al Jazeera StaffPublished On 27 Oct 202627 Oct 2026
United States President Donald Trump has featured a ship he said is carrying Venezuelan oil during a visit to Texas, where he will hold two rallies one after the other in the hopes of boosting Republican chances in a make-or-break Senate race.
Speaking at Corpus Christi on Tuesday on his fourth trip to the state this campaign season, Trump pointed to a ship in the distance.

“It’s got 1 million barrels of oil on it from Venezuela,” he said, adding the cargo was “thanks to our big victory in our recent war with Venezuela”.
The emphasis on the oil comes as US consumers have wrestled with high fossil fuel prices amid the US-Israel war with Iran, a key issue in the upcoming midterm elections.
“We’re celebrating the greatest oil victory in history,” Trump said.
It was not immediately clear under what pretext the oil had been shipped or whether the details Trump gave were correct. The US had received crude oil shipments from Venezuela before the US abduction of Venezuelan leader Nicolas Maduro on January 3, but those transfers have increased this year.

The United States is once again at war in the Middle East, and most Americans say it isn’t worth the cost.

Haidar Yahya Tamimi and his fiancee Ruba were planning to have their wedding this week, before Israel locked down Hebron [Mosab Shawer/Al Jazeera]By Mosab ShawerPublished On 27 Oct 202627 Oct 2026
Hebron, occupied West Bank – Haidar Yahya Tamimi had finished preparing his home, bought new furniture, chosen his wedding suit, and sent invitations to around 1,000 people. After four months of preparations, the 27-year-old was due to marry his fiancee, Ruba, on Friday.
Instead, he has been forced to leave his home in the al-Jalada neighbourhood, and the wedding has been postponed indefinitely.
Recommended Stories list of 3 itemslist 1 of 3Israel’s election: Five key things to knowlist 2 of 3Netanyahu’s pitch: Can Israel use crypto to evade economic sanctions?list 3 of 3Trump says he may move White House press corps to new locationend of list
Haidar is among thousands of Palestinians displaced by an Israeli military operation in Hebron that began after two Palestinian gunmen killed two Israeli soldiers at a checkpoint at the western entrance of the West Bank city on October 23. Both gunmen were killed by Israeli forces.
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu ordered an immediate lockdown in Hebron, and Israeli bulldozers destroyed buildings in the vicinity of the area where the attack took place, as well as going house to house in the neighbourhoods of al-Jalada and Ein Deir Baha, where the attackers lived.
By Monday, more than 3,100 Palestinians had been forcibly displaced, according to Hebron’s municipality.Haidar Yahya Tamimi had his wedding suit ready, but it is now in his home – which he can’t reach because of an Israeli lockdown of his neighbourhood in Hebron in the occupied West Bank [Mosab Shawer/Al Jazeera]

A screengrab from a video posted by US President Donald Trump on September 15, 2025, shows what he said was a US military strike on a boat allegedly carrying drug traffickers in the Caribbean Sea [File: Donald Trump’s Truth Social account/Handout/AFP]By Brian OsgoodPublished On 27 Oct 202627 Oct 2026
The United States military has said that it has killed five people in a strike on an alleged drug trafficking boat in the eastern Pacific, continuing a campaign condemned by legal scholars and rights groups as extrajudicial killings.
US Southern Command (SOUTHCOM), which oversees military operations in Latin America and the Caribbean, said on Tuesday that five people were killed in the strike.

The operation killed five narco-terrorists.”
